regressions.title: Reconnect during preload can bypass the fresh-session inventory wipe
reproduction: Carry a recognizable ordinary item before starting an Attack match.
Disconnect before the preload inventory-clear callback runs.
Reconnect after that callback while the session is still preloading.
Confirm the stale item remains when the match reaches the initial buy phase.
regressions.expected: Every participant entering a fresh Attack session receives the same full inventory reset regardless of reconnect timing.
regressions.observed: The wipe only targets players online at the preload callback, while reconnect and the first buy-phase loadout do not remove ordinary stale items.

regressions.title: Reconnect bypasses an active combat respawn countdown
reproduction: Start an Attack match and die during active combat.
Disconnect while the respawn countdown is running.
Reconnect before the countdown expires.
Confirm the player returns to active gameplay before the original countdown finishes.
regressions.expected: A reconnecting player with a pending respawn stays in spectator/death state until the existing countdown ends.
regressions.observed: CombatTracker restores the countdown, then GameManager restores survival, loadout, and gameplay position about five ticks later.

regressions.title: Six playable arenas expose only two concurrent sessions
reproduction: Prepare valid parties in 3 different Attack arenas.
Start the first 2 arenas so both hold active arena leases.
Ready and start the third arena.
Confirm the third group is queued even though its own visible arena is otherwise available.
regressions.expected: Presented independent arena capacity matches delivered concurrency, or the lower limit is explicitly authored as the player-facing capability.
regressions.observed: Six arenas accept parties, but MAX_CONCURRENT_ARENAS limits active ticking-area leases to two and queues the third session.

regressions.title: Temporary coordinate picker is reachable by normal Creative builders
reproduction: Enter a Build & Decode building phase as the active Creative builder.
Obtain and hold a normal Minecraft stick.
Interact with a block.
Confirm normal interaction is cancelled and coordinate/debug output is shown.
regressions.expected: Temporary coordinate tooling is removed from production or restricted to developer/admin users.
regressions.observed: Any builder holding a normal stick can trigger the imported coordinate picker without an admin requirement.

regressions.title: Capture Run extract gate blocked by unintended fill
reproduction: Start Capture Run Tier 1
Approach the extract-zone entrance
Observe the entrance region before extraction
regressions.expected: The extract-zone entrance remains traversable.
regressions.observed: A spruce-wood fill blocks the entrance and prevents entry.

regressions.title: Arena can restart while its asynchronous world reset is still running
reproduction: Run a Composite arena and change blocks covered by the arena reset.
End or reset the match.
Start the same arena again before reset processing finishes.
Confirm blocks can continue changing underneath the new session during setup or gameplay.
regressions.expected: The arena remains unavailable until its reset finishes, or start admission is blocked by the existing reset lock.
regressions.observed: resetGame starts reset work without awaiting it, then publishes idle state while the reset continues over later ticks.

regressions.title: Cleanup in one arena can invalidate another arena's flag carrier
reproduction: Run Composite Attack concurrently in Arena A and Arena B.
In Arena B, take the red flag and remain alive as its active carrier.
Complete, retry, or reset Arena A so its flag cleanup runs.
Confirm Arena B drops or returns its flag even though its carrier did not die or disconnect.
regressions.expected: Per-arena cleanup changes only the flag carrier state owned by that arena.
regressions.observed: Flag cleanup receives one arena ID but removes the shared carrier tag from every online player in the world.

regressions.title: Arena floor maintenance mutates blocks around unrelated players
reproduction: Keep Player A outside the active Composite arena while standing near dirt.
Start gameplay in Arena B.
Wait for the periodic floor-maintenance interval.
Confirm dirt around Player A changes to grass path despite Player A not belonging to Arena B.
regressions.expected: Periodic arena floor maintenance affects only players and world space owned by that active arena.
regressions.observed: Each active arena runs a grass-path fill as @a, so the mutation executes around players outside the arena too.

regressions.title: Reconnect during preload can carry stale inventory into a fresh session
reproduction: Carry a recognizable non-session item before starting a Composite arena.
Disconnect before the preload inventory clear runs.
Reconnect after the clear while the session is still preloading.
Confirm the stale item remains when preparation or gameplay begins.
regressions.expected: Every player entering a fresh Composite session receives the same full inventory reset regardless of reconnect timing.
regressions.observed: The preload clear only covers online arena players, and later reconnect plus partial loadout refresh does not replay the missed full wipe.

regressions.title: Arena-specific ticking areas are declared but never created
reproduction: Start a Composite Challenge arena and progress to gameplay that spawns or moves entities far from players.
Keep players away from the remote spawn or pathing region.
Continue until the game depends on that distant simulation region.
Confirm remote spawning, pathing, or wave progression can stop because the arena region is not kept ticking.
regressions.expected: Each started arena activates its required simulation regions before gameplay depends on remote chunks.
regressions.observed: Only lobby and permission ticking areas are created; the configured per-arena ticking areas are never materialized.

regressions.title: Arena reset can remove ticking areas from a newly started run
reproduction: Start a Defense match in an arena.
End or reset the match so the arena begins its map reset.
Start a new match in the same arena before reset work finishes.
Confirm the new match loses its arena ticking areas and gameplay simulation can stop.
regressions.expected: An arena becomes reusable only after reset completes, and old cleanup cannot release resources owned by a newer run.
regressions.observed: A new run can reuse the arena before reset finishes, then the old reset releases the ticking-area lease used by the new run.

regressions.title: Reconnect during preload can carry stale inventory into a new match
reproduction: Carry a recognizable non-session item in an inventory slot.
Start a Defense match, then disconnect before the preload inventory wipe runs.
Reconnect after the wipe while the session is still preloading.
Confirm the stale item remains when the new match reaches buy or gameplay phase.
regressions.expected: Every player entering a fresh Defense session passes the same full inventory reset regardless of reconnect timing.
regressions.observed: The preload wipe only affects online players, and reconnect plus later loadout refresh does not clear ordinary items outside managed loadout state.

regressions.title: Reconnect bypasses an active combat respawn countdown
reproduction: Start a Defense match and die during active combat.
Disconnect while the respawn countdown is still running.
Reconnect before the countdown expires.
Confirm the player returns to active gameplay before the original respawn delay finishes.
regressions.expected: A reconnecting player with a pending respawn stays in spectator/death state until the existing countdown ends.
regressions.observed: Combat recovery restores spectator state, then a second reconnect path restores survival, loadout, and gameplay position about five ticks later.

regressions.title: Delayed wave can clear before failed spawn retries finish
reproduction: Reach Defense Level 15, Wave 3.
Trigger the delayed enemy group while its spawn chunk is not ready.
Let the first spawn attempt fail and queue its retry.
Confirm the wave can advance as cleared before the delayed enemies actually spawn.
regressions.expected: A wave remains active while any required enemy spawn is still pending retry.
regressions.observed: Pending group count can reach zero with no live hostiles, so wave-clear logic can run before retry-spawned enemies appear.

regressions.title: Defense reconnect during cutscene loses player loadout

provenance.report: Five Night at Z Village - Level 1 (Defense) - QA

reproduction: Start a Defense match and enter the cutscene
Disconnect during the cutscene
Rejoin the session
Observe the restored gameplay state
regressions.expected: The reconnecting player returns to a valid gameplay state with the intended items and armor.
regressions.observed: A player reconnecting during the cutscene can return without items or armor.

regressions.title: Defense L1 already-owned Iron armor can be purchased repeatedly

provenance.report: Five Night at Z Village - Level 1 (Defense) - QA

reproduction: Purchase or upgrade armor to Iron
Open the gear shop again
Attempt to purchase the same Iron armor tier
regressions.expected: An already-owned armor tier is marked unavailable and cannot consume coins again.
regressions.observed: The same Iron armor upgrade can be repurchased and consumes coins without additional progression.

regressions.title: Defense L1 enchant purchase deducts coins without applying the enchantment

provenance.report: Five Night at Z Village - Level 1 (Defense) - QA

reproduction: Open the enchantment shop with enough coins
Purchase an enchantment
Observe the coin balance and target item/equipment
regressions.expected: Coins are deducted only when the purchased enchantment is successfully applied.
regressions.observed: Coins are consumed but the purchased enchantment effect is not applied.

regressions.title: Defense L1 final lobby countdown does not fully revalidate players

provenance.report: Five Night at Z Village - Level 1 (Defense) - QA

reproduction: Enter the waiting area and begin the final start countdown
Move a required player out of the waiting area during the final seconds
Observe whether the match still starts
regressions.expected: The final countdown revalidates required players and cancels or pauses when start conditions are no longer met.
regressions.observed: The game can still start after a player leaves the waiting area during the final seconds.

regressions.title: Defense L1 bridge-side entity spawn position changes between runs

provenance.report: Five Night at Z Village - Level 1 (Defense) - QA

reproduction: Run the affected bridge-side spawn sequence multiple times
Compare the spawn position between runs
regressions.expected: Entities spawn at the intended location consistently for the same wave/configuration.
regressions.observed: Entities can spawn near the bridge in one run and much farther forward in another.

regressions.title: Defense L1 unloaded spawn chunk can skip waves and produce an early win

provenance.report: Five Night at Z Village - Level 1 (Defense) - QA

reproduction: Progress to Night 4 Wave 2
Allow the configured spawn sequence to execute
Observe spawn success, wave counters, subsequent night progression, and victory state
regressions.expected: Required spawn chunks are loaded before spawn execution, and failed spawns cannot silently advance waves or victory.
regressions.observed: The spawn location can be outside a loaded/ticking chunk, no zombies spawn, later content may be skipped, and the match can reach a win before Night 5 starts.

regressions.title: Defense L1 bridge barrier blocks zombie navigation

provenance.report: Five Night at Z Village - Level 1 (Defense) - QA

reproduction: Reach the bridge-side zombie spawn sequence
Observe zombies moving from spawn toward the objective
Inspect whether the route remains traversable
regressions.expected: Spawned zombies can navigate toward the objective without being blocked by map barriers.
regressions.observed: Zombies become compressed or trapped near the bridge barrier and can die before reaching the intended path.

regressions.title: Defense L2 Builds Shop does not expose configured BuildItems
reproduction: Open the shop
Select Builds Shop
Observe the available build-item offers
regressions.expected: Configured BuildItems are displayed and can be purchased.
regressions.observed: The Builds Shop opens without the intended BuildItems list and only offers a return-to-category action.

regressions.title: Defense L2 flag damage makes the loss condition practically unreachable
reproduction: Allow enemy entities to attack the flag continuously
Observe damage per hit, regeneration, and time required to destroy the flag
regressions.expected: Enemy damage and regeneration allow the flag-destruction loss condition to occur under sustained defense failure.
regressions.observed: The flag takes only 1 damage per hit and regenerates, making destruction extremely unlikely during normal gameplay.

regressions.title: Defense L2 keepInventory gamerule conflicts with intended gameplay
reproduction: Inspect the active gameplay death/inventory behavior
Trigger a player death under normal match conditions
Observe whether inventory retention matches the intended policy
regressions.expected: keepInventory is enabled for the intended gameplay behavior.
regressions.observed: keepInventory is disabled.

regressions.title: Defense L2 Pillager can become stuck near the bridge and delay wave progression
reproduction: Progress to Night 3 Wave 6 or later
Observe Pillager navigation near the bridge-side building
Observe whether wave completion waits on a stuck entity
regressions.expected: Pillagers maintain a valid navigation route and wave completion does not require manual cleanup of stuck entities.
regressions.observed: A Pillager can become stuck on the second floor near the bridge and delay the wave until manually killed or superseded.

regressions.title: Defense L2 time and weather are not locked to the intended environment
reproduction: Play through an active match for enough time to observe world time and weather changes
Observe whether daylight or rain occurs
regressions.expected: Time remains locked to night and weather remains clear during gameplay.
regressions.observed: Time progresses and rain can occur during gameplay.

regressions.title: Active-game reload does not preserve pending wave timeline
reproduction: Start an active level with more than one scheduled wave or a delayed spawn group
Reload scripts/world after the current wave has launched but before the pending delayed group or next wave delay has elapsed
Resume the persisted active session
Observe the delayed group and timing of the next scheduled wave
regressions.expected: Reload reconstructs the active wave timeline, including pending delayed spawn groups and the remaining delay before later waves.
regressions.observed: Recovery rebuilds the scheduler from the next wave index without persisted pending-group/timing state; in-progress delayed groups are not restored and the first resumed future wave is launched immediately.

regressions.title: Six playable arenas expose only two concurrent sessions
reproduction: Prepare valid parties in 3 different Defense arenas.
Start the first 2 arenas so both hold active arena leases.
Ready and start the third arena.
Confirm the third group is queued even though its own visible arena is otherwise available.
regressions.expected: Presented independent arena capacity matches delivered concurrency, or the lower limit is explicitly authored as the player-facing capability.
regressions.observed: Six arenas accept parties, but MAX_CONCURRENT_ARENAS limits active ticking-area leases to two and queues later sessions.

regressions.title: Reconnect during cinematic can carry stale coins into a fresh session

provenance.map: Five Nights at Z Village Level 1

reproduction: Have a party member carry one or more daigon:coin items before starting a new session.
Start the arena and disconnect that player while arena loading is still running.
Reconnect after loading completes while the intro cinematic is active.
Confirm the old coin stack is still available when gameplay begins.
regressions.expected: Every new-session participant has stale inventory and currency cleared regardless of disconnect or reconnect timing.
regressions.observed: The cinematic clear only affects online players, and later kit reconciliation intentionally preserves daigon:coin.

regressions.title: Fall of the Pillager L1 allows teammate damage

provenance.report: Fall of The Pillager - Level 1 (Offense) - QA

reproduction: Start Fall of the Pillager Level 1 with teammates
Attack a teammate during gameplay
Observe whether teammate damage is applied
regressions.expected: Friendly fire is disabled and teammates cannot damage each other.
regressions.observed: Players can hit or damage teammates.

regressions.title: Fall of the Pillager L1 hostile entities keep targeting knocked players

provenance.report: Fall of The Pillager - Level 1 (Offense) - QA

reproduction: Enter combat and become knocked down
Observe hostile entity targeting while the player remains knocked down
regressions.expected: Hostile entities stop targeting the player during the knocked-down state.
regressions.observed: Hostile entities continue targeting and attacking the knocked-down player.

regressions.title: Fall of the Pillager L1 allows self-revive by pre-holding Shift

provenance.report: Fall of The Pillager - Level 1 (Offense) - QA

reproduction: Press or hold Shift immediately before knockdown
Allow the player to enter the knocked-down state
Observe whether the player revives without teammate assistance
regressions.expected: A knocked player can only recover through the intended revive mechanic.
regressions.observed: The player can recover without teammate assistance.

regressions.title: Fall of the Pillager L1 shop UI changes style after returning to menu

provenance.report: Fall of The Pillager - Level 1 (Offense) - QA

reproduction: Open the shop for the first time
Navigate away and use Back to Menu
Compare the returned shop UI with the initial shop UI
regressions.expected: The shop uses a consistent visual hierarchy and presentation across menu states.
regressions.observed: The initial shop UI and the UI after Back to Menu use inconsistent presentation.

regressions.title: Fall of the Pillager L1 upgraded items remain droppable

provenance.report: Fall of The Pillager - Level 1 (Offense) - QA

reproduction: Obtain an upgraded progression item
Attempt to drop the upgraded item from inventory
regressions.expected: Upgraded or progression-critical items cannot be dropped.
regressions.observed: Upgraded items can still be dropped.

regressions.title: Fall of the Pillager L1 can permanently lose the required sword

provenance.report: Fall of The Pillager - Level 1 (Offense) - QA

reproduction: Use the required sword until durability reaches zero
Observe the post-break weapon state
regressions.expected: The intended durability system restores, repairs, or replaces the required sword.
regressions.observed: For some players the sword can fail to return or repair after breaking.

regressions.title: Loadout Trial entity fails to break expected wall
reproduction: Start Loadout Trial level 1
Reach the sequence where the entity should break the wall
Observe entity action and resulting wall state
regressions.expected: The scripted/entity sequence breaks the wall and gameplay can continue.
regressions.observed: The entity does not break the wall and progression is blocked.

regressions.title: Arena 6 is materially incomplete compared with the authored replica
reproduction: Enter or inspect Manhunt Arena 1 and Arena 6.
Compare the corresponding far-side arena region using the authored Arena 6 translation.
Move through the area corresponding roughly to the canonical Z -340 through -220 region.
Confirm substantial geometry present in the canonical arena is missing in Arena 6.
regressions.expected: Arena 6 contains the same gameplay world structure as the canonical arena after the authored translation, aside from bounded intentional differences.
regressions.observed: Native voxel proof finds about 5.62% sampled mismatches in Arena 6, concentrated where thousands of canonical structure blocks are missing as air.

regressions.title: Concurrent arena starts serialize cutscenes across sessions
reproduction: Assign players to separate arenas
Start both arenas at nearly the same time
Observe each arena cutscene lifecycle
regressions.expected: Each arena can start its own cutscene independently.
regressions.observed: Cutscenes behave like a shared queue, leaving one arena apparently unable to start.

regressions.title: Active-game reload recovery aborts the arena
reproduction: Start Orb of the Illusioner Level 2 and reach active Offense gameplay.
Restart the world while the active match is still in progress.
Rejoin after the world finishes loading and wait a few seconds for recovery.
Confirm the arena resets and players return to the lobby instead of the match resuming.
regressions.expected: A persisted active game resumes and reconciles its stage barricades without terminating the arena.
regressions.observed: Scheduled reload validation references undefined selectedBarricades, throws, and sends the active arena into internal-error recovery.

regressions.title: Weapon and armor upgrades consume coins then fail
reproduction: Enter an Orb L2 session and obtain enough coins for a valid weapon or armor upgrade.
Open the normal upgrade UI and buy the next available tier.
Wait for the purchase result.
Confirm the upgrade fails while the spent coins remain deducted.
regressions.expected: A valid upgrade delivers the requested item tier, and any failed delivery leaves the player's coin balance unchanged.
regressions.observed: Coins are consumed before code references an undefined material identifier, causing the upgrade to fail without refund.

regressions.title: Normal gameplay resources expose the production DebugStick
reproduction: Start a Circuit round that grants the normal block resources.
Use 2 supplied oak planks to craft sticks.
Hold or use a stick as a normal non-developer player.
Confirm DebugStick coordinate-selection output appears.
regressions.expected: Production debug interactions are disabled for ordinary players or gated by the existing developer permission owner.
regressions.observed: DebugStickService is initialized in release and handles normal sticks; Circuit supplies oak planks in Survival, making the trigger craftable.

regressions.title: Ordinary players can craft the developer level-skip item
reproduction: Reach Gauntlet Level 13 as a normal non-developer player.
Take oak or dark-oak planks from the authored resource barrels.
Craft a normal Minecraft stick.
Use the stick and confirm the current level is skipped for the arena.
regressions.expected: Level-skip controls are disabled in release or require the existing developer permission before changing progression.
regressions.observed: The stick-triggered skip is enabled without a permission check, and authored Survival resources provide planks that can be crafted into sticks.

regressions.title: Co-op progression can ignore a disconnected required party member
reproduction: Start The Gauntlet with at least 2 players and reach an all-player progression gate such as Level 9.
Disconnect one required party member before the group completes the gate.
Move the remaining online player into the required completion area within the disconnect recovery window.
Confirm the level advances even though the disconnected required member never completed the gate.
regressions.expected: Progression gates requiring the locked party wait for every required member, or pause while one is disconnected.
regressions.observed: The shared all-player predicate filters the locked roster to currently present players before evaluating completion.

regressions.title: Blocked water placement can leave client-only waterlogged residue

provenance.source: Canonical Bug Report V2 + tester runtime evidence

reproduction: Enter a Build & Decode building phase as the active builder.
Use a water bucket against a barrier or another waterloggable block.
Let the map reject the placement.
Confirm only the acting player still sees water or waterlogged residue.
regressions.expected: A rejected water placement leaves no water or waterlogged visual on any client.
regressions.observed: The acting player can retain a water/waterlogged visual after server rejection while other clients do not share the state.

regressions.title: Roommaster/admin bypass can modify protected arena world

provenance.source: Canonical Bug Report V2 + tester runtime evidence

reproduction: Join as the Roommaster/admin role used for map operation.
Move to protected arena geometry outside the active builder plot.
Break a protected block or use a restricted spawn/item interaction.
Confirm the arena world changes despite normal arena protection.
regressions.expected: Roommaster/admin access preserves live arena geometry unless explicit maintenance mode authorizes world mutation.
regressions.observed: Roommaster can destroy protected arena blocks and use restricted spawn/item paths because admin bypasses the arena guards.

regressions.title: Creative-built entities can survive plot reset into later rounds
reproduction: Enter an active round as the builder in Creative mode.
Inside the active build plot, place four iron blocks in a T shape and add a carved pumpkin to create an Iron Golem.
Allow the round to end and the normal plot reset to run.
Start the next round or reuse the same arena.
Confirm the plot blocks are reset but the created Iron Golem can remain because it is outside the cleanup entity allowlist.
regressions.expected: All gameplay-significant mutations that an ordinary builder can create inside the authored plot must either be prevented or included in the arena reset baseline before the next round/session becomes active.
regressions.observed: The builder can create an Iron Golem from ordinary Creative blocks. The reset removes the construction blocks but the entity is not matched by the cleanup allowlist and therefore can remain in the arena after the round.

regressions.title: A fully departed team can remain eligible to win the match
reproduction: Start a team match with at least three active teams.
Let Team A obtain the highest score.
Have every Team A player use Exit to Lobby, or allow them to expire after disconnect, while at least two other teams remain active.
Allow the remaining teams to complete the match without surpassing Team A's score.
Observe that Team A remains in final standings and can be declared/persisted as the winner even though it has no active members.
regressions.expected: A team with no active eligible members after explicit exit or expiry must not remain eligible for the final winner set. Historical contribution may be retained for audit/statistics only if it is explicitly separated from final winner eligibility.
regressions.observed: depart()/expire() remove players from state.members but leave state.players/playerTeams after the match has started. teamStandings() enumerates Object.keys(state.players), and resultFields() derives winnerTeamIds/winnerIds from that historical roster.

regressions.title: Drawn teams are persisted as Wins
reproduction: Start a normal team match with at least two teams.
Finish the match with two or more teams tied for the highest score.
Confirm the match summary/result UI displays Draw.
Open the leaderboard/personal stats after the result is committed.
Confirm players on every tied top team received an additional Win.
regressions.expected: A Draw should preserve the draw result and completed-match/score accounting without incrementing the persistent Win counter for every tied team, unless the product intentionally defines a draw as a win everywhere.
regressions.observed: The result presentation says Draw while all tied leading teams are written as winners and each tied player gains +1 Win. Persistent Wins can then affect leaderboard ordering.

regressions.title: Creative equipment can persist across role changes, exit and replay
reproduction: Enter an active round as the builder in Creative mode.
Equip a Creative-obtained armor/chest/offhand item, for example an Elytra or shield.
Finish the round so the player becomes a guesser, or use Exit to Lobby and then join another session.
Observe the normal inventory cleanup/role transition.
Confirm the equipped item is not owned by clearInventory() and can remain equipped across the transition.
regressions.expected: Role/session cleanup must restore the complete managed player state, including equipment/offhand acquired during Creative builder access, before the player becomes a guesser, returns to lobby or starts another session.
regressions.observed: clearInventory() removes inventory container slots only. No gameplay cleanup path clears minecraft:equippable slots, while builder Creative access allows equipment acquisition and use.

regressions.title: Guess action temporarily disables Exit to Lobby
reproduction: Enter an active guessing phase with both Guess and Exit to Lobby items available.
Use the Guess item.
Immediately switch to Exit to Lobby and attempt to use it within two seconds.
Confirm Exit remains on the shared cooldown instead of being independently usable.
regressions.expected: Guess anti-spam cooldown should not disable the player's independent Exit to Lobby control.
regressions.observed: Both builddecode:guess and builddecode:exit_game use cooldown category wind_charge for two seconds, so activating one temporarily cools down the other.

regressions.title: Time bonus thresholds do not match the authored scoring table
reproduction: Start a normal Build & Decode match and reach an active guessing round.
Make a correct guess within 8 seconds and compare the awarded time bonus with the Points.timebonus table.
Repeat with a correct guess at 16-25 seconds and at 31-50 seconds.
Confirm the effective bonuses are +5, +2, and 0 instead of +10, +3, and +1.
regressions.expected: Time bonuses follow the selected artifact's Points.timebonus table: +10 through 8s, +5 through 10s, +4 through 15s, +3 through 25s, +2 through 30s, +1 through 50s, then 0.
regressions.observed: The scoring function gives +5 instead of +10 through 8s, +2 instead of +3 from 16-25s, and 0 instead of +1 from 31-50s. These points feed player/team scores and can change standings and persisted leaderboard results.

regressions.title: Final round publishes a next-round transition before terminal eligibility is decided
reproduction: Play through the final playable round.
Observe the round-end HUD.
Check whether it says 'Next round in …' even though the match ends after that countdown.
regressions.expected: Terminal eligibility is decided before transition messaging, so the final round communicates match completion rather than a nonexistent next round.
regressions.observed: The round-end owner unconditionally publishes 'Next round in …'; only after the countdown does prepareRound()/selectRound() determine there is no next round and call finish().

regressions.title: Settled match result is only published through chat while authored final-result UI is disconnected
reproduction: Complete a normal match.
Observe the terminal result presentation.
Check whether a dedicated winner title/final standings UI appears before reset.
regressions.expected: After exact-once result settlement, the settled result is presented through the authored terminal-result surface before cleanup/return.
regressions.observed: finish() settles the result and publishes matchSummary() through chat, then resets. showFinalStandings() exists but has no production caller, and the terminal path has no winner title or victory sound.

regressions.title: Deferred victory can race timeout and settle one attempt twice
reproduction: Reach the flag capture boundary as the level timer reaches zero.
Allow the capture path to queue victory while timer expiry resolves timeout.
Observe whether the same attempt can receive both terminal outcomes or an invalid completion duration.
regressions.expected: Exactly one terminal outcome owns each attempt; later terminal callbacks for the same attempt are rejected without mutating result, score, feedback, or transition state.
regressions.observed: Timeout can clear attempt timing state before a previously queued victory callback executes; because terminal ownership is not locked, the delayed victory can subsequently be accepted.
